name: Together Code Sandbox

modes.label: Code Sandbox VMs on a Together custom plan (sales only; self-serve = codesandbox-sdk card)
modes.commit_note: Only on Together custom (sales) plans; contract fee/minimums unpublished.
modes.note: Sales-only: Code Sandbox is "currently available on Together's custom plans"; "a self-serve option is possible by creating an account with CodeSandbox" (https://docs.together.ai/docs/together-code-sandbox, 2026-09-28). Self-serve pricing for the same VMs lives on the codesandbox-sdk card; this mode is not duplicated here. Rates kept for reference only: together.ai/pricing lists $0.0446/vCPU-h + $0.0149/GiB-h (2026-09-28). Sold only on the custom plan (fee unpublished), so the row stays unpriced. Billed per started minute on the allocated tier (alloc).

modes.label: Together Code Interpreter ($0.03 per 60-minute session)
modes.note: Hosted Python execution API: $0.03 per session, session lifespan 60 min, reusable across many executions (state/packages persist). CPU/RAM/disk unpublished (vcpu/ram null). Self-serve on prepaid Together credits. Not a general VM: no custom image, Docker or inbound ports. Re-verified 2026-09-28: "$0.03/session", 60-minute lifespan, reusable (https://docs.together.ai/docs/together-code-interpreter; together.ai/pricing "Session (60 minutes) $0.03"). Not flagged alt: it is a code-interpreter product and ranks as one.
plans: Together pay-as-you-go (prepaid credits; Code Interpreter only)

plans.name: Together custom plan (Code Sandbox)
plans.note: Code Sandbox is 'currently available on Together's custom plans'. Custom concurrency; credit discounts negotiated.

plans.name: Together pay-as-you-go (prepaid credits; Code Interpreter only)
plans.note: Prepaid, $5 minimum credit purchase; API suspended at zero balance; auto-recharge optional; credits never expire. Only the Code Interpreter mode is self-serve on Together.

perf_source: No benchmark row: provider is not in ComputeSDK results or the HPC run (as of 2026-09-28). See research/perf-map.json.

knobs.label: Idle tail before the VM hibernates (× session hours)
knobs.why: Code Sandbox VMs are the CodeSandbox VMs: credits burn on the allocated tier by wall-clock while running, including the idle tail until hibernationTimeoutSeconds; hibernated VMs consume no credits. Default 1 = hibernated/shut down when work ends; the 2x ceiling is a judgment call.

caveats: The VM mode is sales-only (Together custom plans) and restricted to that plan, so it is not priced here; the self-serve route to the same VMs is the codesandbox-sdk card (Build free / Scale $170). The former bulk-credit mode (assumed 50% off, from CodeSandbox Enterprise) was removed: it duplicated codesandbox-sdk pricing on a guess.

Two price expressions for the same VMs: per-resource list rate ($0.0446/vCPU-h, $0.0149/GiB-h) vs CodeSandbox credit tiers ($0.01486/credit); they agree within ~0.1% on 2 GB/core tiers. Only fixed tiers actually exist.

Code Interpreter: $0.03 per 60-min session, resource spec unpublished (sizes vcpu/ram null). Self-serve on the pay-as-you-go plan; not flagged alt. Session state persists within the hour; billed per session not per call.
Together is fully prepaid ($5 minimum, no free trial credit); API suspended at zero balance.
Storage (hibernation snapshots), egress, IPv4 pricing not published (null). Hibernated VMs consume no credits in CodeSandbox's model.
perf null: benchmarks.json has no together-code-sandbox entry; same infrastructure as providers.codesandbox (cold start 2,329 ms, burst 7,658 ms, dax 81.2 s).

Hibernated sandboxes are kept on disk up to 7 days, then may be archived to long-term storage (resume 20-60 s instead of 0.5-2 s). No storage fee for hibernated/archived state is published (snapshot_gib_month stays null).

Official sources disagree on the smallest tier and credit price: Together docs and codesandbox.io/docs list Pico = 2 cores / 1 GB at $0.01486/credit ($0.0743/h), while codesandbox.io/pricing lists Pico = 1 core / 2 GB and credits at $0.015 (Nano $0.15/h, 'Without subscription savings'). The Together per-resource list rate prices Pico (2c/1GB) at $0.1041/h, 40% above the credit price; it matches the credit price only on 2 GB-per-core tiers.

fleet.tiers: Self-serve via CodeSandbox SDK: Build free 10 concurrent / 20 creates per hour; Scale ($170) 250 concurrent / 1,000 creates per hour; Together custom plan (CodeSandbox Enterprise) custom concurrency and 'Create as many Sandboxes as you need'.
fleet.notes: Self-serve path is a codesandbox.io workspace: concurrent VM Sandboxes Build 10 / Pro 10 / Scale 250 / Enterprise custom; new SDK sandboxes per hour Build 20 / Pro 20 / Scale 1,000 / Enterprise custom; SDK requests per hour 1,000 / 1,000 / 10,000 / custom. On the Together custom plan (= CodeSandbox Enterprise) all three are negotiated. The previous '50 Scale, 300/1,000 custom' figures are not on any live page. Together Code Interpreter has no published session/concurrency cap.
fleet.create_rate_limit: CodeSandbox SDK: 20 new sandboxes/hour (Build, Pro), 1,000/hour (Scale), custom (Enterprise = Together custom plan); SDK API 1,000 / 1,000 / 10,000 requests/hour / custom

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: By default, when a Sandbox is hibernated, a memory snapshot is created. This allows for near-instant resumes the next time the Sandbox is accessed—typically within 0.5–2 seconds.
snapshot_auto.note: Trigger: inactivity timeout (hibernationTimeoutSeconds, default 300 s free / 1800 s pro, max 86400 s; SDK source: 'the amount of seconds the sandbox will be kept alive without activity before it is automatically hibernated'). Memory + disk included; kept on disk up to 7 days, then may be archived (disk only, 20-60 s resume, setup tasks rerun). Optional automatic wake-up on HTTP/WebSocket.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Memory snapshot/restore (checkpointing) at any point in time.
snapshot_on_demand.note: Memory included. SDK: sandboxes.hibernate(id) snapshots the whole VM on demand; sdk.sandboxes.create({id}) forks a new sandbox from a template or existing sandbox ('A template is a memory/fs snapshot of a Sandbox'), so new machines can boot from it (running processes continue). Templates built via CLI.

harness_api.note: SDK clients are File System, Terminals, Commands, Interpreters, Ports, Hosts, Tasks, Setup; no agent-harness driver. 'Agent' in the SDK refers to CodeSandbox's in-VM Pitcher agent, not an AI harness.

ingress_rules.quote: private: Sandbox is private, hosts require tokens
ingress_rules.note: Privacy per sandbox: public, private (hosts need host tokens via signed URL, headers or cookies), public-hosts (default). Browser Preview API restricted to workspace-configured trusted preview hosts (regex). No IP allowlists; all ports get hostnames.

guest_firewall.note: Each sandbox is a Firecracker VM with root; note the user environment runs in a Docker container inside the VM (CLEAN boot: start Firecracker VM, then start the Docker container), so rules may need to be applied at the VM level; not documented.

secret_proxy.note: Credentials are passed into the sandbox: session env vars and a git accessToken in SessionCreateOptions. No credential-injecting proxy documented.

nested_virt.quote: Under the hood, the SDK uses the microVM infrastructure of CodeSandbox to spin up sandboxes.
nested_virt.note: derived: sandboxes are themselves Firecracker microVMs; no /dev/kvm, KVM, or nested-VM capability is documented anywhere in the SDK docs, API reference, or openapi.json (no 'kvm'/'nested' hits). Docker/Dev Containers run inside the VM, but that is container isolation, not nested hardware virtualization.

browser.quote: Together Code Sandbox offers a fully configurable development environment with fast start-up times, robust snapshotting, and a suite of mature dev tools.
browser.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. This is a general dev-environment/code VM (Firecracker microVM with terminals, commands, filesystem, ports, Docker) with no managed/real browser instance for the agent to drive; no Chromium/Playwright/Puppeteer mention anywhere in the SDK or CodeSandbox docs.

anti_bot.quote: Run generative code tooling in fast, secure sandboxes at scale.
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Together Code Sandbox is a code-execution/dev VM product, not a browser-automation/scraping product; no stealth/fingerprinting features are documented.

captcha_solving.quote: Run generative code tooling in fast, secure sandboxes at scale.
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No CAPTCHA-solving capability is documented for this code/dev-VM product.

ssh.quote: The Terminals API allows you to create, manage and interact with terminal processes in your sandbox.
ssh.note: No SSH access is documented anywhere in the SDK docs, API reference, or openapi.json (no 'ssh' hits). Interactive shell access is exposed only via the SDK's own WebSocket-based Terminals/Commands API, not standard SSH.

volume_attach.quote: We persist the workspace folder and the Docker engine state, like images, volumes, etc.
volume_attach.note: Persistence is the VM's own workspace disk (and Docker's internal named volumes inside that disk); there is no documented API to attach a separate, independently provisioned persistent volume to a sandbox.

volume_shared.quote: Everything in your workspace is guaranteed to persist between reboots, hibernations and forks.
volume_shared.note: No mechanism is documented for mounting one volume across multiple simultaneously running sandboxes; each VM has its own private workspace disk.

live_resize.quote: You can change the VM specs of a running sandbox by calling the sandbox.updateTier method... This will change the VM specs of the sandbox dynamically, without rebooting.

own_agent_api.quote: Run generative code tooling in fast, secure sandboxes at scale.
own_agent_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. The SDK exposes filesystem/terminal/command/port primitives for running your own code/agent, not a first-party browser/computer-use/research task agent that Together or CodeSandbox drives itself.

egress_allowlist.quote: sandboxes.create / sandboxes.update options cover privacy, vmTier, hibernationTimeoutSeconds, automaticWakeupConfig, ipcountry — no egress/network-policy fields.
egress_allowlist.note: No outbound allow/deny-list, no-internet mode, or security-group egress control is documented in the SDK docs or the openapi.json spec (no 'egress'/'allowlist'/'firewall' hits).

egress_http_rules.quote: sandboxes.create / sandboxes.update options cover privacy, vmTier, hibernationTimeoutSeconds, automaticWakeupConfig, ipcountry — no egress/network-policy fields.
egress_http_rules.note: No HTTP method/path-level egress rules are documented; only inbound host privacy (public/private/public-hosts) is controllable.

static_egress_ip.quote: sandboxes.create / sandboxes.update options cover privacy, vmTier, hibernationTimeoutSeconds, automaticWakeupConfig, ipcountry — no egress/network-policy fields.
static_egress_ip.note: No fixed/static outbound IP feature is documented (consistent with the card's ipv4_available: false, no published IPv4 pricing).

open_source.note: Only the client-side @codesandbox/sdk library (the API wrapper/CLI) is MIT-licensed; the underlying Firecracker microVM orchestration platform that actually runs the sandboxes is closed-source, and CodeSandbox explicitly states self-hosting is not offered ('Is it possible to self-host CodeSandbox SDK? No, we do not offer self hosting at this time.', sdk/faq.mdx).

hipaa.quote: For customers with data-residency, regulatory, or compliance requirements... Together supports private networking and VPC-based deployments, including in EU regions.
hipaa.note: Together publishes HIPAA-attested cluster placement only for its model-inference dedicated endpoints ('--placement.hipaa' restricts deployment to HIPAA-attested clusters); no HIPAA-eligibility or BAA is documented for Code Sandbox / the CodeSandbox VM platform.

eu_data_residency.quote: ipcountry: This determines in which cluster, closest to the given country the VM will be started in. The format is ISO-3166-1 alpha-2. If not set, the VM will be started closest to the caller of this API.
eu_data_residency.note: Sandbox creation accepts an ISO-3166-1 country code to place the VM in the nearest cluster to that country, letting a caller target an EU country; not an explicit region/data-residency guarantee, but functionally lets EU customers keep sandboxes on EU-proximate infrastructure.

max_session_h.quote: hibernation_timeout_seconds: The time in seconds after which the VM will hibernate due to inactivity. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 86400.
max_session_h.note: The only documented cap (86400 s = 24 h) is an idle/inactivity hibernation timeout, configurable and pausable, not a hard maximum on total running/session time; a VM Sandbox can otherwise be kept running or repeatedly resumed indefinitely (fork_running, wake_on_request, pause_resume are all supported).

desktop.quote: Fast, secure code sandboxes for AI development and agent workloads. Instant VM creation with snapshotting, flexible vCPU and memory scaling, persistent storage with git version control, DevContainer support, terminal access, task execution, and preview hosting.
desktop.note: Product is a headless microVM for code execution (terminal/commands/fs/ports only, per the SDK docs). No VNC/RDP/streamed GUI desktop offered anywhere in the docs or SDK client list.

computer_use.quote: Under the hood, the SDK uses the microVM infrastructure of CodeSandbox to spin up sandboxes... It supports: Memory snapshot/restore (checkpointing)... VM FS persistence... Environment customization using Docker.
computer_use.note: No desktop exists (see desktop claim), so there is no screenshot+click driving API. SDK surfaces are fs/terminals/commands/interpreters/ports/hosts/tasks/setup only.

volumes.quote: VM FS persistence (with git version control).
volumes.note: Persistence is the sandbox's own root filesystem (persistent_disk, already true on the card), not a separate attachable/shareable volume resource. No volume-attach or multi-mount API documented.

public_ipv4.quote: Connecting Sandboxes in the browser... In addition to running your Sandbox in the server, you can also connect it to the browser.
public_ipv4.note: Ports are exposed via CodeSandbox preview hostnames/tokens (see ingress_rules evidence: 'private: Sandbox is private, hosts require tokens'), not a per-machine public IPv4. Card's network.ipv4_available is already false; no IPv4 offering found anywhere.

agent_harnesses.note: Same evidence already on the card for harness_api: SDK clients are File System, Terminals, Commands, Interpreters, Ports, Hosts, Tasks, Setup - no preinstalled/templated coding-agent harnesses (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode) documented.

gpu.quote: Together Code Sandbox can spin up a sandbox by cloning a template in under three seconds. Inside this VM, you can run any code, install any dependencies, and run servers.
gpu.note: Firecracker microVM sizes go up to 64 vCPU/128 GiB per the card's custom-plan mode; no GPU tier is listed on together.ai/pricing or in the docs, and no GPU appears in CodeSandbox's own VM tier tables.

windows.quote: Whenever a sandbox boots from scratch, the platform will: 1. Start the Firecracker VM 2. Create a default user (called pitcher-host) 3. (optional) Build the Docker image specified in the .devcontainer/devcontainer.json file 4. Start the Docker container
windows.note: Firecracker only runs Linux guests; the boot sequence (Docker container inside the VM, Dev Containers) is Linux-only. No Windows guest option documented.

macos.quote: Under the hood, the SDK uses the microVM infrastructure of CodeSandbox to spin up sandboxes.
macos.note: Firecracker microVMs are Linux-KVM based and cannot run macOS guests; no macOS option anywhere in the docs.

arm64.note: No CPU architecture choice is published anywhere (only vCPU/RAM tiers); Together/CodeSandbox docs never mention ARM or Graviton instances, so no evidence an ARM64 option exists.

self_host.quote: Code Sandbox is a Together product that is currently available on Together's custom plans. A self-serve option is possible by creating an account with CodeSandbox.
self_host.note: Access is only via Together's hosted custom plan or a CodeSandbox.io hosted account/API token - there is no self-hosted/on-prem deployment option documented.

byoc.quote: Code Sandbox is a Together product that is currently available on Together's custom plans. A self-serve option is possible by creating an account with CodeSandbox.
byoc.note: Only two access modes exist (Together custom plan or CodeSandbox.io account), both running on Together/CodeSandbox-owned infrastructure/clusters; no deploy-into-customer-cloud-account option documented.

egress_ip_type.quote: ipcountry: This determines in which cluster, closest to the given country the VM will be started in. ... If not set, the VM will be started closest to the caller of this API.
egress_ip_type.note: Together Code Sandbox VMs run on CodeSandbox's own Firecracker microVM cloud infrastructure, placed in regional clusters selectable by country hint; no residential/mobile/ISP proxy IP product is mentioned anywhere in the Together or CodeSandbox docs, SDK reference, or openapi.json (no 'residential'/'proxy'/'mobile IP' hits). This is a standard multi-tenant cloud VM egress path, i.e. datacenter IPs, not a stated 'static' per-VM IP (card's static_egress_ip is already false).
